title: Samsung Galaxy Tab Active4 Pro 5G 64GB Rugged Tablet with S Pen $593 + Delivery @ MyITHub
body:
Deal: Samsung Galaxy Tab Active4 Pro 5G 64GB Rugged Tablet with S Pen $593 + Delivery @ MyITHub

[RichardL] FWIW, this tablet was released in 2022.
Also might struggle with 4GB of RAM.
[myithub] Fair points. Yes, this model was released in 2022, and the 4GB RAM/64GB storage configuration isn’t aimed at gaming or heavy multitasking.
The main value is for field service, logistics, warehouses and other work environments where the rugged construction, IP68 rating, removable battery, 5G, NFC, Samsung DeX and included S Pen are more important.
We should have made the model age and intended use clearer in the description—thanks for pointing it out.
[RichardL] Also worth noting that Samsung Galaxy Tab Active4 Pro doesn't receive anymore Android Updates (ending on OneUI 7.0/Android 15) and only ~a years left on Security updates.
[Droider95] Not worth it.
Rather buy the A11+
11" Screen 1920 x 1200
Samsung Dex Support

[koplik88] I've been looking at tablets online. I have an alldocube but the battery is on the way out. It looks like this one is wi-fi only
[eug] Totally different use case. If you're after a general purpose tablet for home use, the A11+ makes more sense. If you're after a rugged tablet, this makes more sense.
If you don't need a rugged tablet, don't buy a rugged tablet. If you need a rugged tablet, don't buy an ordinary tablet.
[Tehcookiemonsta] Quite sure you could buy like an otterbox case or lifeproof case for a tablet and while it may not offer the exact same protection it would be far better value…
[eug] and while it may not offer the exact same protection it would be far better value…
If you don't need a rugged IP68 tablet, don't buy a rugged IP68 tablet.
If you need a rugged IP68 tablet, don't buy a cheap tablet and put it in a case and hope it lasts like a rugged IP68 tablet.
[IXXI] I have 2 of these that are used regularly in semi-rugged environments. Great workhorse. I've destroyed normal tablets in rugged housings, but these have held up well. Old, yes. Somewhat outdated, yes. But for their intended purpose, at this price, not behd!
[myithub] Thanks for sharing your real-world experience. That’s exactly the intended use case—these aren’t the newest or fastest tablets, but they’re built to survive environments where standard tablets, even with rugged cases, may not last. Glad to hear yours have held up well.
[Craypot] These are aimed at the likes of installing navigation software like Navionics for yachting.
I've drowned a few phones using them whilst sailing.
The active 4 is on my list. Just not sure how bright the screen is on the 22 model, and I prefer the smaller 8"version.
I'm also looking at the Ulephone rugking as a cheaper option.
How's the screen brightness on this one OP?
[Craypot] Me mate google tells me 550 nits, good but not awesome in direct sun on deck
[LukeOz83] Thats like last century specs. Similar to my Intel Core Duo
